tagline: The slow road north, beside I-75, through the Thumb's farm towns.
intro: M-15 starts on the northwest edge of metro Detroit at Clarkston and heads north, running roughly parallel to I-75 but taking its time about it. Past Clarkston it narrows to two lanes and goes by the lakes around Ortonville, then on through Goodrich, Davison, Otisville and Millington to Vassar, where it crosses the Cass River and turns northwest across the farmland to Bay City.
On the first Saturday in May the stretch from Clarkston to Vassar turns into one long yard sale.

moments.title: Clarkston
moments.text: The road comes up Main Street through the Clarkston Village Historic District, in the village the Clark brothers platted in 1842.

moments.title: Ortonville
moments.text: Amos Orton founded the village in 1848 by damming Kearsley Creek to run his gristmill.

moments.title: Vassar
moments.text: Named for a founder's uncle, Matthew Vassar, who went on to found Vassar College, the town lost the county seat to Caro in 1860 and went on lumbering.

sources.label: MDOT, Pure Michigan Byways Driving Guide (Wayback Machine snapshot, December 2025)
